confidence_semantics: publisher/source authority only; not parcel numeric accuracy

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR web-service URL persistence announcement
verified_facts: EA announced persistent non-year-specific LIDAR service URLs for future updates, including the Composite DTM 1m WCS.
EA notes ArcGIS WCS compatibility/rendering limitations and publishes national raster display statistics as rendering aids.
semantic_limits: Service persistence is endpoint governance, not parcel lineage or elevation evidence.
National rendering statistics must never be used as target elevation values or parcel extrema.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Retired LIDAR Composite DTM 2017 - 25cm
verified_facts: EA marks the 2017 25cm Composite DTM as retired and no longer available on DSP, replaced by the 1m composite.
The retired dataset documents historical composite resampling, ODN reference and metadata-index lineage practice.
semantic_limits: A retired 25cm composite must not override the current 1m primary-product contract.
Historic resolution does not imply current target coverage or parcel-specific accuracy.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model 10m
verified_facts: EA states the 10m DTM is resampled from the Composite DTM 2m using bilinear interpolation.
It is a bare-earth model aligned to the OS National Grid and referenced to Newlyn, with source-survey lineage inherited from the composite chain.
semantic_limits: The 10m product is too coarse and derived to replace the primary 1m parcel sample.
Its lineage is correlated with other EA composite products rather than independent validation.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Catalogues
verified_facts: EA publishes a catalogue dataset described as indices for full-coverage LIDAR surveys of England.
The catalogue record links to composite terrain and surface datasets.
semantic_limits: Catalogue existence is discovery/provenance context only.
It does not satisfy an exact target feature/intersection or numeric raster sample gate.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 Documentation root
verified_facts: OS describes Terrain 5 as a detailed bare-earth DTM of Great Britain supplied as grid and contour data at five-metre intervals.
The current documentation states quarterly publication and routes users to overview, technical specification, downloads and known-issues resources.
semantic_limits: Documentation-root summaries are product context, not parcel measurements.
Terrain 5 remains secondary to EA DTM1m for this workflow.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 Documentation root
verified_facts: OS describes Terrain 50 as an open height dataset covering Great Britain with grid and contour forms.
The current documentation states annual July updates and 50m grid spacing.
semantic_limits: Documentation freshness is not a target-tile certificate.
Terrain 50 remains coarse correlated secondary evidence.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 National Grid tile reference
verified_facts: OS states Terrain 5 is divided into 5km-by-5km tiles identified from the National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
The documented reference scheme uses the 100km grid letters plus 10km digits and a quadrant suffix such as NE, NW, SE or SW.
semantic_limits: A syntactically valid tile reference is not proof of a parcel intersection or data availability.
Tile naming is packaging/location context, not height accuracy.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 product supply
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is supplied as a full Great Britain tile set with 5km-by-5km data tiles and accompanying metadata files.
OS states quarterly full-tile resupply in January, April, July and October.
semantic_limits: Release cadence is not the flying/survey date for a target tile.
Full-tile resupply does not create independent evidence from metadata and terrain values within the same product.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 data structure
verified_facts: OS states Terrain 5 grid height values are calculated at pixel centres.
For tidal water, tile-average mean-water values and interpolation can introduce a small discrete step between adjacent tiles.
semantic_limits: Pixel-centre values are not parcel-boundary extrema without polygon sampling.
Tidal-tile edge effects must not be mistaken for a real terrain discontinuity without contextual validation.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 product supply
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 tiled formats are supplied as a national set of 10km-by-10km tiles; GeoPackage/vector-tile variants can be single national files.
OS states annual full-tile resupply in July.
semantic_limits: Packaging format and annual release date are not target observation dates.
Multiple encodings remain correlated representations of the same OS terrain source.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 data structure
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 grid heights are calculated at pixel centres and have no shared edge values between adjacent raster tiles.
OS documents possible small discrete tidal-height steps between adjacent tiles and notes spot heights are interpolated-source features not guaranteed to be summits.
semantic_limits: Tile-edge differences and spot heights must not be promoted to parcel extrema without geometry-aware checks.
These are product-model semantics, not independent measurements.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 grid data specification
verified_facts: OS specifies a 200-by-200 ASCII raster for each 10km tile with 50m cells and centre-calculated values.
Height values are stored to the nearest 0.1m and the companion GML provides spatial/vertical-reference metadata.
semantic_limits: 0.1m encoding precision is not 0.1m physical accuracy.
Terrain 50 cell values remain coarse secondary cross-checks rather than parcel extrema.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 Esri Shapefile structure
verified_facts: OS documents contour/tide line and spot-height shapefile components plus per-tile metadata files.
Projection information is supplied in .prj files.
semantic_limits: Shapefile is an encoding of the Terrain 50 contour supply, not an independent terrain source.
Metadata/flying-date fields do not turn contour points into primary parcel samples.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 GeoPackage structure
verified_facts: OS supplies Terrain 50 contours as a national GeoPackage with spot_height, land_water_boundary and contour_line layers.
The GeoPackage uses user-friendly attribute naming but represents the same terrain contour content.
semantic_limits: A different container/attribute naming scheme is not independent validation.
GeoPackage contour content remains secondary and correlated with other Terrain 50 encodings.

candidates.name: Guidance for preparing plans for HM Land Registry applications
verified_facts: HMLR requires application/deed plans to allow the land to be clearly identified on the Ordnance Survey map and provides preferred plan scales and mapping-detail guidance.
For unusual extents such as airspace/subsoil, the guide recognises use of Ordnance Survey Datum to define vertical extent; this is a legal-plan description context rather than a terrain dataset.
semantic_limits: A compliant application plan is not proof of an exact registered boundary unless the register/determined-boundary evidence establishes it.
Use of OS Datum in a deed plan does not replace official DTM sampling for terrain-height difference.

candidates.name: Preparing plans for HM Land Registry applications publication
verified_facts: The official PG40 supplement 2 publication page records the current guidance as last updated 13 October 2025.
It identifies the guidance as the HMLR deed-plan preparation supplement.
semantic_limits: Publication freshness is provenance context only.
It supplies no parcel geometry or elevation measurement by itself.
